newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU slaps anti-dumping duties on Chinese handbags.
newsitem.headline: EU slaps anti-dumping duties on Chinese handbags.

text.p: The European Commission has introduced anti-dumping duties of nearly 40 percent on imports of handbags from China, according to the Official Journal available on Wednesday.
Following a complaint launched in March last year by the European Committee for Leather Goods Industries, the Commission said it had evidence Chinese manufacturers were dumping handbags in Europe.
The Journal said EU handbag production soared from 33.5 million units in 1992 to 40 million units last year, but sales had dropped by 12 percent in the same period.
It said the EU imported 89 million handbags from China last year -- 43 percent more than in 1992 -- and that Beijing's market share increased from 51 percent to 60 percent.

The Journal said Chinese handbag manufacturers had "significantly undercut Community producer's prices, eroding profitability and causing a gradual reduction in employment as well as a number of company closures".
Two Chinese manufacturers were excluded from the 39.2 percent duty introduced. Lee and Man Handbags Manufacturing Ltd will pay just 30.7 percent while Jane Shilton (Pacific) Ltd will pay no duties.
Both companies cooperated with the Commission probe, the Journal said. -- David Fox, Brussels Newsroom ++ 32 2 287 6832
